newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY LEAGUE-SOUTH WALES PULL OUT LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-SOUTH WALES PULL OUT LEAGUE.

text.p: South Wales, denied a place in the European Super League, have pulled out of Britain's Rugby Football League (RFL), the RFL said on Wednesday.
The Cardiff-based club, who played in division two in their first season this year, were felt not to be ready for the Super League and instead were offered a place in division one for 1997.
But South Wales told the RFL it was Super League or nothing for them.
RFL chief executive Maurice Lindsay said: "They felt that division one would be a halfway house and that people in South Wales want to watch the best or nothing.
"I'm personally disappointed because I was a big fan but they still have plans to apply for Super League for either 1998 or beyond."
